dialect.detail: IBM mainframe QSAM file processing style with RECORDING MODE IS F, BLOCK CONTAINS 0 RECORDS, LABEL RECORDS ARE STANDARD; French comments suggest possible European mainframe environment

purpose.domain_detail: Streaming/media subscription service - merging customer profile data with watch/viewing history records
purpose.summary: This batch program merges two sequential QSAM files: a CUSTOMER-FILE (customer profile data including account, name, subscription info) and a WATCH-FILE (viewing history with content ID, watch percent, media type) into a single MERGED-FILE. It performs a sequential merge by accountNumber, reading both files and writing combined records.

notable_features: RECORDING MODE IS F on all files
PERFORM UNTIL with dual EOF flags
Sequential merge algorithm comparing account numbers
INVALID KEY clause on sequential WRITE (unusual/incorrect usage)
No COMP-3 usage despite numeric-like fields stored as PIC X
verdict.notes: The use of INVALID KEY on a sequential WRITE is technically incorrect (INVALID KEY applies to indexed/relative files); this suggests a student or learning exercise. French comments ('Programme COBOL de traitement de fichiers QSAM', 'Déclaration des fichiers') indicate a French-speaking developer. The merge logic has potential issues: when EOF conditions are met, the PERFORM UNTIL loop may still attempt processing. No COMP-3 or numeric PIC clauses used despite numeric data fields. The domain appears to be a streaming/media service based on field names (watchPercent, mediaType, contentId, subscriptionProgram).
